home.unitTitle: A gentle start to the day
home.mascotGreeting: Nice to see you! Shall we start slowly?
home.advisoryBody: Short activities help you revisit the day and gather memory cues. A little each day is enough.

speech.listeningBody: Take your time and speak slowly. Tap the button below when you finish.
speech.unsupported: Speech recognition is limited on this device. You can type your answer in the box below.
speech.durationHint: Speak comfortably for about 20 seconds. If it runs long, it wraps up on its own.

routine.memoryDay: A day to gently wake memory
routine.languageDay: A day to wake up talking
routine.dailyFlowDay: A day to organize the day's order
routine.moodDay: A day to recall mood and company
routine.reviewDay: Light review and a garden reward

weekly.title: Keep it going this week
weekly.completedDays: You kept it going {{count}} day(s) this week.
weekly.catalogNote: Small rewards at welfare centers are decided by the operating organization.
weekly.bragCard: {{count}} days of memory routine this week

support.title: Counseling resources
support.body: If worries repeat, organize the activity records and notes, then contact a nearby official counseling resource. This is not a diagnosis or screening result.
support.verifyNote: Phone numbers and addresses are shown only after verifying against the organization's latest official information.
support.pending: Official counseling contacts for this region appear after the latest verification.

review.topic: Last time, which topic did you choose for your memory?
review.topicExplanation: That's right. You chose a memory about {{topic}}.
review.emotion: Do you remember how you said you felt then?
review.emotionExplanation: Yes, you said you felt {{emotion}} then.
review.people: In the memory you saved last time, who was with you?
review.place: Do you remember where that memory happened?

story.people: Who was with you in the story you shared last time?
story.place: Which place appeared in the story you shared last time?
story.object: Which object was a cue in the story you shared last time?
story.emotion: Which feeling was closest to the story you shared last time?
story.time: Which time cue appeared in the story you shared last time?
story.summary: Which story is closest to the memory you shared last time?

story.label: My Story
story.helper: Leave concrete memory cues you can revisit later.
story.speakBody: Press speak and talk comfortably for about 20 seconds.
story.unsupported: Speech recognition is limited in this browser. You can leave the story in the box below.
story.placeholder: Example: Last spring, I went to the hospital with my daughter and ate soup nearby. It rained, and I felt grateful because she brought an umbrella.
story.privacy: Personal stories are private by default and are not shared with family unless you choose to share them.

cognitive.wordRecallEncodeGuide: Remember each word together with its category. You will choose the same words again later.
cognitive.wordRecallRecallGuide: Choose the {{count}} words you saw at the beginning. Mistakes are stored only as practice-flow records.
cognitive.wordRecallFreeHelper: Write the words that come to mind first, then confirm with the choices below.
cognitive.digitSpanBackwardGuide: Look at the numbers in order, then tap them backward on the next screen.
cognitive.verbalFluencyGuide: A routine for recalling words within one topic.
cognitive.verbalFluencyIntro: The timer will start when you begin. Type words separated by commas, or say them aloud and enter what you remember.
cognitive.trailGuide: Follow the highlighted next cue and alternate between numbers and pictures. If you tap the wrong item, you can continue right away.
cognitive.trailWrongNode: Try the displayed next cue instead of {{label}}.
cognitive.orientationGuide: A light start-of-day routine for checking today's date and weekday.
cognitive.stroopGuide: Read slowly and tap the visible ink color while setting aside the word meaning.
cognitive.stroopEmpty: No color cards are ready for this routine.

start.title: Ready to start today’s memory routine?
start.description: Try a few short activities to gently revisit today.
start.todayPhrase: Small, steady effort helps each day feel clearer.
start.hint: Take it slowly, one step at a time.
start.mascotMessage: When you’re ready, tap Start. The routine is short and easy to follow.

garden.subtitle: A garden where your own memories grow.

family.title: Caregiver Report
family.subtitle: Review shared memories and activity patterns from a caregiver view.
family.inviteBody: Family members or caregivers can review shared memory cards and activity summaries.
family.privacyBody: Memory cards are private by default. Only items chosen by the user are shared with family.
family.summaryEmpty: There is no activity to share yet. Keep practicing gently.
family.loggedInModeLabel: Haru caregiver and counselor demo account
family.demoModeNote: Example report built from 30 days of activity records and shareable memory cues.

conversation.noPrivateDetailsNote: Personal memories that the user did not share are not shown in caregiver or counselor views.

observation.title: Caregiver Observation Notes
observation.body: If family members notice changes over the last few weeks or months, record a short note before the next conversation.
observation.notePlaceholder: Example: Appointment times need more reminders, but the walking routine is still steady.
observation.supportNote: A caregiver note for organizing everyday changes before a care conversation.

report.routineTrendUp: Participation in the last 7 days is higher than the previous 7 days. Continue with gentle encouragement.
report.routineTrendDown: Participation in the last 7 days is lower than the previous 7 days. Suggest an easy restart without pressure.
report.routineTrendFlat: Participation has not changed much in the last 7 days. Keep a short routine at a familiar time.

strengths.routines: {{count}} activities have been completed so far.
strengths.consistency: About {{completionRate}}% of recorded activities were completed, showing routine participation.
strengths.reviewCadence: There are no memory cards due right now, so conversation can stay light.
strengths.routineMomentum: Recent participation is increasing, so brief encouragement may help.
strengths.gentleStart: There is limited data so far. Support a comfortable start rather than evaluation.

activityHighlights.wordRecall: In the latest word-recall routine, {{count}} word(s) were selected again.
activityHighlights.digitSpan: The latest number-memory routine reached {{length}} digit(s).
activityHighlights.verbalFluency: The latest category-speaking routine recorded {{count}} unique word(s).
activityHighlights.trail: The latest attention-switching routine had {{count}} retry tap(s).
activityHighlights.stroop: The latest color-focus routine recorded {{correctCount}} focused tap(s), {{errorCount}} other tap(s), and an average response of about {{averageSeconds}} second(s).
activityHighlights.orientation: The latest date-awareness routine checked today's date and weekday.
activityHighlights.drawing: The latest drawing routine recorded {{strokeCount}} stroke(s) over about {{seconds}} second(s).
activityHighlights.fallback: There are recent activity records, but detailed cues are still limited.

nextTopics.shareableSeed: Start by saving one short memory the user is comfortable sharing.
nextTopics.topic: Prepare a light question from {{count}} saved memory item(s) about {{topic}}.
nextTopics.reviewDue: {{count}} memory card(s) are due today and can be used as conversation starters.
nextTopics.routineConsistency: If participation decreased, suggest restarting with the easiest activity rather than asking why.
nextTopics.routineMomentum: Recent participation is increasing. Encourage the same short routine at a familiar time.
nextTopics.prepareConversation: Use shared memories to ask about one specific scene before the conversation.
nextTopics.observationDailyRoutine: Ask which familiar routine still feels easiest, and which step may need a small cue.
nextTopics.observationConversation: Prepare slower, concrete questions if recent conversation flow looked different.
nextTopics.observationAppointments: Check whether calendar reminders, appointment cards, or a same-day call would help.
nextTopics.observationNavigation: Ask about familiar places and plan one simple route cue together.
nextTopics.observationMedicationMoney: Review whether medicine, bills, or payment steps need a shared checklist.
nextTopics.observationMoodSocial: Prepare a gentle question about mood, contact with others, or activities they still enjoy.
nextTopics.observationSleepAppetite: If sleep or meal rhythm looks different, ask which part of the day felt most comfortable.
nextTopics.observationHomeSafety: Review home movement paths, lighting, and where frequently used objects are placed.
nextTopics.observationUncertain: For areas marked not sure, use a neutral check-in question rather than drawing conclusions.

summary.steady: The current records show a flow that can continue with low pressure.
summary.watch: {{signalCount}} support signal(s) suggest a calm follow-up conversation.
summary.needsConversation: {{signalCount}} support signal(s) overlap, so a caregiver or counselor should prepare a concrete conversation.

dataCompleteness.limited: There are still only a few records, so interpret lightly.
dataCompleteness.usable: Several days of activity can support conversation preparation.
dataCompleteness.rich: Multiple weeks of activity and observation records can be reviewed together.

domainSummaries.steady: {{domain}} has no prominent support signal right now.
domainSummaries.withSignals: {{domain}} has {{count}} support signal(s), reviewed at the {{level}} level.

signals.participationStopped: No activity was recorded in the last 7 days, after {{previous}} attempt(s) in the previous 7 days.
signals.participationLower: Recent 7-day attempts decreased to {{recent}}, compared with {{previous}} in the previous 7 days.
signals.wordRecallLow: Recent word recall selected {{correct}} of {{target}} words again.
signals.wordRecallWatch: Recent word recall selected {{correct}} of {{target}} words, which can guide the next memory conversation.
signals.digitSpanMisses: Number memory practice recorded {{count}} re-check selection(s).
signals.digitSpanShort: Recent number memory practice stayed around {{length}} digits.
signals.verbalFluencyLow: Category word practice recorded {{count}} unique word(s).
signals.colorFocus: Color focus practice recorded {{errors}} other choice(s), averaging about {{seconds}} seconds.
signals.orientationMismatch: Date and weekday practice recorded a mismatch.
signals.drawingHesitation: Drawing practice recorded {{clearCount}} clear action(s) and about {{seconds}} seconds of activity.
signals.observationUncertain: Caregiver note marked {{domain}} as '{{response}}', so use a neutral check-in.

nextSteps.keepRoutine: Continue short routines around the same time and build positive memory cues.
nextSteps.prepareConversation: In the next conversation, ask about a recent easy activity and a specific moment that felt harder.
nextSteps.memoryCue: Use shareable memory cards to revisit one person, place, or feeling at a time.
nextSteps.simplifyRoutine: If attention or drawing signals appear, reduce instructions and offer one activity at a time.
nextSteps.caregiverCheck: Compare caregiver notes with real daily scenes in a calm family conversation.
nextSteps.professionalConversation: If concerning patterns repeat, organize activity records and caregiver notes for a professional conversation.

family.counselorSubtitle: Use recent activity and shared memories to prepare the next conversation.
family.counselorDisclaimer: This screen is a reference report for preparing care and counseling conversations, based on demo activity records.

cues.fallbackEasiest: Ask which activity felt easiest during the last 30 days.
cues.fallbackTomorrow: Ask what activity or memory topic they might want to try again tomorrow.
cues.askSummary: Ask which scene feels most vivid from the recent shared story: '{{summary}}'.
cues.askEmotion: Ask why they felt '{{emotion}}' then, and who comes to mind with that feeling.
cues.askPeople: Ask whether they remember another pleasant moment with '{{person}}'.
cues.askPlace: Ask what they would want to do first if they visited '{{place}}' again.

settings.autoStartTitle: Open today's routine right away on start

onboarding.title: Welcome
onboarding.welcomeBody: Pick a few things at your own pace and today's routine will start right away.

step.largeTextHint: Turning large text on makes the words clearer.
step.inputModeTitle: How would you like to take part?
